question: A 27-year-old woman goes to the genetic counseling clinic after having a child with Down syndrome. In the child, a trisomy 21 with translocation 21/21 inherited from the mother is identified. What would be the risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in the future children of this woman?

options.opa: The risk of recurrence will be 10-15%, as in the rest of translocations.
options.opb: 100% of viable fetuses will be born with Down syndrome.
options.opc: The risk of recurrence will be very low (12%).
options.opd: The risk of recurrence will be 50%.

analysis: In cases of Down syndrome caused by a Robertsonian translocation involving chromosome 21, the risk of recurrence can be significantly higher than in standard trisomy 21 cases. If the mother is a carrier of a translocation involving chromosome 21, the risk of having another child with Down syndrome can be as high as 50% for each pregnancy, depending on the specific nature of the translocation. Therefore, the correct answer is that the risk of recurrence will be 50%.
